**6/9/2026 5-Day Incident Report**
On June 4, 2026, the customer called Kia's Customer Care Center to report an accident involving her 2022MY Kia Sorento. Specifically, the customer stated, "I [was] driving with cruise on at 55mph, approached a yield and oncoming car did not yield, I slammed on my brakes, I hit a truck from behind." She reported that she was transported to the hospital with a broken left arm and cuts/bruises on her legs and chest. The customer wanted to know why her airbags did not deploy and requested compensation.  

The subject Kia Sorento is equipped with Lane Following Assist ("LFA") and Smart Cruise Control ("SCC"). LFA is a supplemental system that helps to detect lane markings and/or vehicles on the road and assists the driver's steering to help keep the vehicle between lanes. SCC is a supplemental system that detects a vehicle ahead and can help maintain the distance from the vehicle ahead and the set speed. The functionality of LFA and SCC are contingent upon several outside factors, and it is always the responsibility of the driver to safely steer the vehicle, to maintain the vehicle in its lane, and to maintain the vehicle's speed.

The customer stated that she "slammed on my brakes" and hit the oncoming vehicle that had failed to yield. Kia notes that once the brakes are applied, the SCC system is no longer operating at Level 2 as such feature would be overridden. Based on the customer's description of the incident and her request to Kia, there is nothing to suggest that the vehicle's ADAS Level 2 features malfunctioned.

**9/15/2026 Monthly (September) Update Report**
On August 13, 2026, Kia's Safety Office inspected the subject vehicle and downloaded the EDR report, which was reviewed on August 24, 2026. The driver frontal, driver knee, passenger side, and passenger curtain airbags deployed along with both front seat pretensioners. The passenger frontal airbag deployment was suppressed because the driver was the only occupant in the vehicle. Smart Cruise Control (SCC) was active and engaged at 57 mph and operating normally before the crash. The brakes were pressed at 1.0 second before the crash, which cancelled the SCC system, and Anti-lock Brake System (ABS) activated at 0.5 seconds before the crash. No issues with the vehicle ADAS or restraint systems were identified.
